column1: Watashi wa taitei asa hachiji goro okiru.
column2: I usually wake up around 8 a.m.
column3: 私はたいてい朝八時ごろ起きる
column6: 私|は|たいてい|朝|八時|ごろ|起きる
column8: Okiru is a ru-verb in its dictionary / plain nonpast form. Here it describes a routine, not a past event.

column1: Sorekara, tsumetai shawaa o abite, asagohan o tabete, basu de shigoto ni iku.
column2: Then I take a cold shower, eat breakfast, and go to work by bus.
column3: それから冷たいシャワーを浴びて朝ご飯を食べてバスで仕事に行く
column6: それから|冷たい|シャワー|を|浴びて|朝ご飯|を|食べて|バス|で|仕事|に|行く
column8: Abiru → abite; taberu → tabete: te-forms link actions. Iku at the end sets the nonpast tense of the sequence.

column1: Gogo wa konpyuutaa de muzukashii mondai o toku.
column2: In the afternoon, I solve difficult problems on the computer.
column3: 午後はコンピューターで難しい問題を解く
column6: 午後|は|コンピューター|で|難しい|問題|を|解く
column8: Toku means solve; it is a u-verb. De marks the tool, the computer; o marks the problems being solved.

column3: 仕事は忙しくて大変だ
column6: 仕事|は|忙しくて|大変|だ
column8: Isogashii → isogashikute joins an i-adjective to another description. Taihen is a na-adjective; da is the plain ending.

column1: Sorekara, tomodachi to koohii o nomi ni itte, kyuukei suru.
column2: Then I go drink coffee with friends and take a break.
column3: それから友達とコーヒーを飲みに行って休憩する
column6: それから|友達|と|コーヒー|を|飲み|に|行って|休憩|する
column8: Nomu → nomimasu → nomi (stem) + ni expresses purpose. Iku → itte links going to kyuukei suru, taking a break.

column2: The coffee is cold and delicious.
column3: コーヒーは冷たくておいしい
column6: コーヒー|は|冷たくて|おいしい
column8: Tsumetai → tsumetakute joins two descriptions. The final adjective oishii sets the tense.

column1: Gogo goji made ni ie ni kaeru.
column3: 午後五時までに家に帰る
column6: 午後|五時|まで|に|家|に|帰る
column8: Made ni means by a deadline; ni after ie marks the destination. Kaeru is a u-verb despite ending in eru.

column1: Soshite, atatakai bangohan o tabete, tomodachi to tanoshii terebi geemu o suru.
column2: Then I eat a warm dinner and play fun video games with friends.
column3: そして温かい晩ご飯を食べて友達と楽しいテレビゲームをする
column6: そして|温かい|晩ご飯|を|食べて|友達|と|楽しい|テレビ|ゲーム|を|する
column8: Taberu → tabete links eating to playing. To marks companions; o marks the object of each activity.

column1: Demo, watashitachi wa geemu ga amari jouzu janai.
column2: But we aren’t very good at games.
column3: でも私たちはゲームがあまり上手じゃない
column6: でも|私たち|は|ゲーム|が|あまり|上手|じゃない
column8: Amari pairs with a negative: not very. Jouzu is a na-adjective; jouzu janai means not good at.

column2: On weekends, I go to the gym.
column8: Wa presents weekends as the time topic. Ni marks the destination; iku is plain nonpast.

column2: Then I hang out with friends.
column8: To marks who you spend time with. Asobu is a u-verb meaning play / hang out.
